subject.title: [Feature] Queue prompts when API limits prevent an immediate response

question: Should OpenClaw core own a durable SQLite-backed capacity-wait prompt queue for provider API-limit pauses, and should the partial followup/provider PRs be folded into that design?
rationale: The requested behavior spans durable runtime state, provider cooldown semantics, visible session state, and replay guarantees, so automation should not choose the product boundary or storage contract from the existing partial PRs alone.

options.title: Sponsor a core design
options.body: Keep #49251 as the canonical tracker and require a SQLite-backed core queue design that coordinates or supersedes the partial followup and provider-cooldown PRs.

options.title: Narrow to followup restart only
options.body: Let #82572 or a similar PR solve only restart persistence for followup queues and leave provider API-limit capacity-wait queuing for a separate future issue.

options.title: Reject core queuing
options.body: Close the request as out of scope for core and require providers/plugins or clients to handle capacity waiting outside OpenClaw orchestration.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core design
recommendation.body: Keep #49251 as the canonical tracker and require a SQLite-backed core queue design that coordinates or supersedes the partial followup and provider-cooldown PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the queue, model fallback, and runtime paths that this product choice crosses.
